title: Quantify quality-adjusted latency (QAL) across proxy-driven batching and prefix-cache deltas
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Objective: Run a controlled sweep to measure the tradeoff between end-to-end latency and output quality when changing batching and prefix/KV cache configurations. Introduce a composite metric, Quality-Adjusted Latency (QAL), that normalizes observed quality regressions against latency improvements to help make rollout decisions for runtime config changes. This ticket scopes the experiment design, testbed runs, and the initial analysis that will feed the rollout gating criteria.

Motivation: We routinely adjust batching and KV cache heuristics to reduce per-token cost and P50/P95 latency, but customers have reported subtle quality regressions for some prompt shapes (especially short-turn dialogues and instruction-following prompts). Existing evals measure latency and quality separately; teams need a single signal that captures the practical tradeoff (small quality regressions vs meaningful latency wins).

Scope:
- Implement proxy-based synthetic load harness that can replay a realistic per-tenant sequence length distribution (including short-turn and long-turn mixes).
- Sweep batching parameters: microbatch_size, continuous_batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens.
- Sweep KV cache behaviors: prefix_ttl, cache_eviction_policy, cache_key_shard_count.
- Evaluate across 3 model variants: rwi-open-13b-fp16, rwi-open-13b-4bit, rwi-instruct-7b-quant (to capture quantization interactions).
- Use adversarial prompt subset (instruction microbench) + representative production prompt set for quality checks.
- Compute QAL and visualize Pareto front to select candidate configs for canary.

Deliverables:
1) Test harness and orchestration config (k8s job + proxy runner) checked in.
2) Evaluation notebooks and a reproducible pipeline that runs nightly against a stable commit.
3) Dashboard tile showing QAL, delta-quality, median latency, P95 latency, token cost for each config.
4) Recommendation document (pass/fail gates) for config rollout to canary and Dedicated customers.
test_plan: 1) Deploy proxy harness to staging and validate request fidelity vs production traces (compare seq-length histograms)
2) Run baseline (current production config) for 24h synthetic replay to get noise floor
3) Sweep each axis independently then run combined grid for Pareto analysis

4) For each run capture: median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_consumed, cost_estimate, quality_metrics (BERTScore, exact-match for slot-filling tests, and instruction-following accuracy), and QAL
5) Validate stability by repeating top-3 promising configs for 3 independent runs
results_summary: Initial baseline run completed 2026-03-05. Observations: (a) Increasing continuous_batch_window_ms from 15ms to 60ms reduced median latency by 12% on long-turn workloads but increased instruction-following failure rate by 1.8% on the adversarial subset; (b) enabling aggressive prefix_ttl=120s reduced token cost by ~9% for conversational workloads but introduced cache-key aliasing edge cases causing rare hallucination-style artifacts in 0.2% of samples; (c) QAL ranking favored a conservative batch window (30ms) + prefix_ttl=300s for most models, but 4-bit quantized variant showed higher sensitivity to batch size changes. Full numeric CSV uploaded to the linked Drive doc.
next_steps: 1) Run 3-repeat validation for top-2 QAL configs across the three model variants by 2026-03-12
2) Create a canary release plan and rollback criteria if QAL drops by >0.02 relative to baseline
3) Add tokenization-aware sampling to the proxy harness to capture microbatch boundary artifacts
4) Draft runtime config gating rules for Console UI (recommend default values and advanced flags)
